nodes.summary: Two words $x, y$ of length $n$ agree in exactly $n - \Delta(x, y)$ coordinates, where $\Delta$ is the Hamming distance. The proof of the Johnson bound counts agreements rather than disagreements.
nodes.title: Agreements of two words

nodes.summary: Let $Q \in F[X][Y]$ be nonzero with $(1, w)$-weighted degree at most $D$, where $w \ge 1$. At most $D / w$ (integer division) polynomials $P \in F[X]$ have $Y - P(X)$ dividing $Q$: each such $P$ is a root of $Q$ viewed as a polynomial in $Y$ over the integral domain $F[X]$, and $Q$ has $Y$-degree at most $D / w$. This bounds the size of the list output by the Guruswami–Sudan decoder.
nodes.title: The list has at most $D / w$ polynomials

nodes.summary: Under the hypotheses of the Johnson bound ($e \le n$, $d \le n$, words pairwise at distance at least $d$, all within distance $e$ of $y$, and $n(n-d) < (n-e)^2$), the set has at most $n d$ words: the denominator $(n-e)^2 - n(n-d)$ is a positive integer and the numerator $n (d - e)$ is at most $n d$.
nodes.title: Johnson bound, list size $n d$

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha_1, \dots, \alpha_n \in F$ be distinct, $1 \le k \le n$, $y \in F^n$, and $t \le n$ with $t^2 > n (k - 1)$. Every finite set of polynomials of degree less than $k$, each agreeing with $y$ in at least $t$ positions, has at most $n (n - k + 1)$ elements.
nodes.title: Reed–Solomon codes are list decodable up to the Johnson radius

nodes.summary: There are $r(r+1)/2 = \binom{r+1}{2}$ monomials of total degree less than $r$: $s + 1$ of each total degree $s < r$. So a root of multiplicity $r$ at one point imposes $\binom{r+1}{2}$ linear constraints on the coefficients of $Q$.
nodes.title: Number of multiplicity constraints

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha_1, \dots, \alpha_n \in F$ be distinct and $y \in F^n$. Let $Q \in F[X][Y]$ have $(1, w)$-weighted degree at most $D$ and a root of multiplicity at least $r$ at every point $(\alpha_i, y_i)$. If $P \in F[X]$ has degree at most $w$ and $P(\alpha_i) = y_i$ for $t$ indices $i$ with $t r > D$, then $Q(X, P(X)) = 0$; equivalently $Y - P(X)$ divides $Q$.
nodes.title: Guruswami–Sudan root-finding lemma

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a field, $(\alpha_1, y_1), \dots, (\alpha_n, y_n) \in F^2$, and $w, D, r$ natural numbers. If the number of monomials $X^i Y^j$ with $i, j \le D$ and $i + w j \le D$ exceeds $n \cdot r(r+1)/2$, there is a nonzero $Q \in F[X][Y]$ of $(1, w)$-weighted degree at most $D$ with a root of multiplicity at least $r$ at every point $(\alpha_i, y_i)$.

nodes.summary: If the translate $Q(X + a, Y + b)$ has no monomial of total degree less than $r$, then $Q$ has a root of multiplicity at least $r$ at $(a, b)$, that is $Q \in (X - a, Y - b)^r$.
nodes.title: Multiplicity from the translated coefficients

nodes.summary: A bivariate polynomial $Q \in F[X][Y]$ has a root of multiplicity at least $r$ at $(a, b)$ if $Q$ lies in the $r$-th power of the ideal of the point $(X - a, Y - b)$.

nodes.summary: If a code is list decodable from $e$ errors with list size $L$, it is list decodable from $e$ errors with every list size $L' \ge L$.
nodes.title: List decodability is monotone in the list size

nodes.summary: Let $C$ be a code of length $n$ whose distinct codewords are at Hamming distance at least $d \le n$, and let $e \le n$ satisfy $n(n-d) < (n-e)^2$, that is $e < n - \sqrt{n(n-d)}$. Then $C$ is list decodable from $e$ errors with list size $n d$.

nodes.title: List-decodable code

nodes.title: Johnson bound

nodes.summary: The pairs $(u, v)$ of natural numbers with $u + v < r$, grouped by the total degree $s = u + v$: the exponents of the monomials $X^u Y^v$ whose coefficients in the translate of $Q$ must vanish for a root of multiplicity $r$.
nodes.title: Monomials of low total degree

nodes.summary: If $Q(X, Y)$ has $(1, w)$-weighted degree at most $D$ and $P \in F[X]$ has degree at most $w$, then $Q(X, P(X))$ has degree at most $D$: each monomial $X^i Y^j$ becomes $X^i P(X)^j$, of degree at most $i + w j$.
nodes.title: Substitution respects the weighted degree

nodes.summary: For $a, b \in F$, the ideal $(X - a, Y - b)$ of $F[X][Y]$, generated by $X - a$ and $Y - b$: the polynomials vanishing at $(a, b)$. Its powers measure the multiplicity of a root.
nodes.title: Ideal of a point of the plane

nodes.summary: If $Q(X, Y)$ has a root of multiplicity at least $r$ at $(a, b)$ and $P \in F[X]$ satisfies $P(a) = b$, then $(X - a)^r$ divides $Q(X, P(X))$.
nodes.title: A root of multiplicity $r$ survives substitution

nodes.summary: For $a, b \in F$, the $F$-algebra automorphism $Q(X, Y) \mapsto Q(X + a, Y + b)$ of $F[X][Y]$. A root of $Q$ at $(a, b)$ becomes a root of the translate at the origin, which is how Guruswami, Rudra and Sudan define multiplicity at a general point (Definition 12.2.9).
nodes.title: Translation of the plane

nodes.summary: A bivariate polynomial $Q(X, Y) = \sum_{i,j} q_{ij} X^i Y^j$ over a field $F$ has $(1, w)$-weighted degree at most $D$ if $i + w j \le D$ for every monomial $X^i Y^j$ with $q_{ij} \ne 0$. For $w = 1$ this is the total degree.
nodes.title: Weighted degree bound

nodes.summary: Under the hypotheses of the root-finding lemma, $Y - P(X)$ divides $Q(X, Y)$ in $F[X][Y]$. So Step 3 of the Guruswami–Sudan algorithm, which factors $Q$ and keeps the factors $Y - P(X)$ with $\deg P < k$ close to the received word, finds every polynomial that agrees with the received word in more than $D / r$ positions.
nodes.title: $Y - P(X)$ divides the interpolating polynomial

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
